authorization: Explicit user response: Approve the scoped refusal exception (Recommended).
scope: Only newly implemented I9-7 routes whose stock success callback is unsafe on an error-only HTTP 200 body; includes the unaccepted I9-7A task refusal repair. Other accepted families keep their contracts.
rules: R1 A reachable refusal may return HTTP 400 with an error-only body and no nonempty error_msg when HTTP 200 would dispatch the stock success callback. Preserve safe stock-specific error handling where it is actually present.

R2 Success remains HTTP 200 with genuine owner state. Malformed or forged requests remain HTTP 400; internal failure remains HTTP 503. Refusals must not fabricate successful state, charge, grant or advance gameplay.

R3 A6 success probes still require HTTP 200. Declared refusal probes may require HTTP 400, but must demonstrate no Lua success-branch error or false successful client transition. Native refusal, exact retry, concurrency, journal and stock UI reachability requirements remain mandatory.
R4 Current source/effective client is preserved. This exception does not authorize a global Backend.lua patch, waive missing assets, declare a blocked scenario passed or close a stage.
R5 Claude registers this approved scoped exception and its evidence at I9-7 qualification; the implementation checkpoint does not supersede selected seal 793.
